title: Edgekeeper control pad: streamlined reserve controls and health signals for Dedicated GPU pools
creator: Olivia Chen
description: Design a compact, operator-focused control pad for Dedicated GPU pool owners that surfaces health signals, allows quick autoscale and burst tuning, and provides safe fallbacks for production workloads. This ticket covers a prototype for a right-rail control surface (Edgekeeper) that sits on the pool detail page and acts as the primary quick-action UI for on-call engineers and platform operators. Goals: 1) Reduce time-to-triage by surfacing a 10s glance view of health signals (latency p50/p95, queue depth, KV cache hit rate, memory pressure). 2) Provide contextual single-click actions: apply conservative burst, enable predictive autoscale, pause new job placement (safeguard), and roll back to last-stable model/variant. 3) Include inline explanations and safe defaults to avoid accidental cost spikes. Scope excludes backend autoscale algorithm changes; this ticket focuses on UX, microcopy, interaction states, and prototype handoff to frontend.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype for Edgekeeper integrated on pool detail page, responsive to narrow and wide layouts
Interaction spec documenting states for actions (confirm, cooldown, success, error) and permission gating (SRE vs owner)
Accessible color palette and token mapping consistent with Console design system
Usability test notes from at least 5 operators proving the 10s-glance reduces triage time compared to current console
Handoff package with annotated components, copy snippets, and a small set of API contract examples for frontend (action endpoints, expected responses)
comments: 2025-02-16 - Olivia Chen: Kickoff with SRE and Product. Identified top metrics operators want at a glance — p95 latency, queue length, recent autoscale events, and billing burn rate. SRE emphasized safe defaults; Product asked for quick rollback affordance.

2025-02-20 - Liam Rodriguez: Uploaded initial lo-fi sketches (edgekeeper-wireframe-v1). Proposed a vertical affordance: header (pool name, status), compact sparkline row, primary action stack, and a small telemetry detail expander.

2025-02-24 - Maya Patel (SRE): Review notes — preference for a 'Pause new allocations' toggle instead of full stop button; request that burst application include a cost estimate modal. Also flagged RBAC requirements (only pool admins can scale).

2025-02-26 - Ben Soto (Product): Added acceptance scenario for 'rollback to last-stable variant' and requested confirmation microcopy. Suggested integration with Rollouts feature to show canary status before applying actions.

2025-02-28 - Liam Rodriguez: Uploaded hi-fi prototype (edgekeeper-pad-v2.fig) and interaction spec. Included microcopy for confirmation dialogs and cooldown timers. Noted two unknowns: (1) exact error responses from autoscale API, (2) cost estimate calculation input fields. Both flagged for ENG.

2025-03-01 - Olivia Chen: Usability session scheduled for 2025-03-05 with 6 participants (SREs and Platform Engineers). Updated prototype based on internal review; changed burst slider to discrete preset chips (conservative, moderate, aggressive) per feedback to reduce decision fatigue.
